import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Calculate total sales for each product and size
# Group by product and size, then sum the 'total' column
sales_by_product_size = df.groupby(['product', 'size'])['total'].sum().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Define a preferred order for sizes for consistent stacking and legend
# This also ensures only existing sizes are considered
preferred_sizes_order = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']
available_sizes = [s for s in preferred_sizes_order if s in sales_by_product_size.columns]
sales_by_product_size = sales_by_product_size[available_sizes]

# Sort products by their total sales (sum across all sizes) for better readability
sales_by_product_size['total_product_sales'] = sales_by_product_size.sum(axis=1)
sales_by_product_size = sales_by_product_size.sort_values(by='total_product_sales', ascending=False)
# Drop the temporary column used for sorting
sales_by_product_size = sales_by_product_size.drop(columns='total_product_sales')

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create the stacked bar chart
sales_by_product_size.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, cmap='viridis', ax=plt.gca())

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Size', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability, especially if product names are long
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Add a legend, placing it outside the plot area to avoid obscuring data
plt.legend(title='Size', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Improve layout to prevent labels, title, or legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
